plain: A result that follows naturally from something proved.

webster.text: A conclusion or consequence drawn from premises, or from what is advanced or demonstrated.

example.quote: and from it I draw one corollary, which, I think, clearly follows, although it is in favor of the Constitution, to wit — that at least that clause in which Congress guaranties to the several states a republican form of government, speaks honestly ;
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 2, New York Convention, July 2, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
